To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) GDDs provide an improved interface to decision diagrams (2) the improved interface can significantly reduce the clutter in code (3) the improved interface, in combination with the use of FIDDs for encoding asynchronous transition relations, permits the creation of novel algorithms for asynchronous model checking that are more efficient and easier to understand than existing algorithms (4) the use of GDDs, in combination with a new parallel version of the TeDDY library, will enable scalable parallel decision diagram manipulation

we have developed new foundations for implicit encoding that enable the creation of new model checking algorithms with a significantly improved interface to the TeDDy library, and we are exploring how to improve the performance and scalability of model checking via parallelization of the resulting system.

(1) GDDs provide a new compact form of DD, with the desirable properties of FIDDs and closure over all DD operators, and (2), the novel library interface, using C+ metaprogrmming, provides a clean high level interface to TeDDys GDD library.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality of model checking research by orders of magnitude.

developing a new interface to TeDDY, which will permit users to create novel, efficient model checking algorithms, while automatically generating efficient code having the performance and compactness of existing hand optimized TeDDy code.
improving the efficiency, quality, and speed of model checkers for concurrent systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

I will develop a new decision diagram encoding, GDDs, that are more efficient and easier to use than FIDDs, and will develop a novel interface to TeDDY, using C+ metaprograms, that permits users to write efficient algorithms without resorting either to library modifications or to low level manipulation of concrete data structures.
I propose to demonstrate the advantages of C+ metaprograms, in terms of both performance and convenience in writing research code, by using them to create a new TeDDy library interface.

I have invented a novel interface to TeDDY, that I have proven the correctness of GDDs, that I will demonstrate the utility and convenience of the improved interface, that I will explore the use of the improved library to create new fully symbolic model checking algorithms and that I will explore using novel heuristics to obtain scalable parallelism in the manipulation of decision diagrams, and in model checking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new library interface will permit the writing of C++ algorithm code in a much less cluttered style while automatically generating code with performance similar to that of existing hand optimized decision diagram code.
we have created an efficient and convenient library interface to decision diagrams, that is well defined, and supports efficient parallel manipulation of decision diagrams.

the proposed system will support convenient construction of parallel model checking software, while obtaining significant parallel speed ups, and will be used to improve the performance, by orders of magnitudes, of existing model checking algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a well defined interface to an improved underlying data structure, and the use of a parallel execution environment, will enable the development of significantly improved algorithms for model checking asynchronous systems, and significantly improved research in model checking.

the new GDDs, and the novel interface to TeDDY, are a significant improvement to the current state of the art, and will enable a significant improvement in the performance and quality of model checking research.

the use of C+ metaprograms to create a novel interface, to TeDDy (and similar libraries) can significantly improve the quality, speed, and convenience, of research in symbolic model checking, and other areas.
